title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 3 part 2a: treating a cheap model's error as independent noise gives an exact expected count of full DFN runs, which plans screen-versus-GP-EI right on 14 of 16 pool sizes (worst-case bound: 8) but cannot rank SPMe, whose errors sit on particular designs; milestone 3: a proved bound shows a cheap screen's cost in full DFN runs is bounded by its residual after an affine fit, which ranks 11 screens at Spearman 0.72 (raw error -0.07), and SPMe's residual tracks its own salt depletion (-0.82); milestone 4: replaying 12 searches on the cached benchmark, screening every candidate with the plain SPM or a 2-cycle DFN run reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best about 30% faster than GP-EI on DFN (153 to 168 s vs 220 s on pools of 64), the 10-cycle DFN screen is slower (253 s) and GP-EI catches up by 96 designs; milestone 2: a 10-cycle DFN run ranks designs by 100-cycle DFN energy at Spearman 0.96 against 0.64 for 100-cycle SPMe at the same cost; milestone 1: SPMe's own minimum salt concentration flags the designs it mis-scores (AUC 0.997) (modelled, PyBaMM OKane2022, stack level)
summary: A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 3 (theory, part 2a) treats the screen’s residual as independent noise and gives an exact expected count of DFN runs (a one-dimensional integral for Gaussian noise). As a planner it calls whether whole-pool screening beats GP-EI right on 14 of 16 (screen, pool size) cases, against 8 of 16 for the worst-case formula; with one whole-space noise level it ranks the 11 screens only at Spearman 0.51 (refuted), 0.86 with the noise level near the top, because SPMe’s large errors fall on particular designs (on the DFN-best ones at 100 cycles: 14 DFN runs needed, 3 predicted). Milestone 3 (theory, part 1) proves that screen-then-verify needs at most as many full DFN runs as there are designs within 2κ of the best, where κ is the screen’s worst residual after the best affine fit, so scale and shift errors are free; the bound held on all 330 (screen, pool) cases. Across 11 screens κ ranks the DFN calls needed at Spearman 0.72, the raw error at −0.07; SPM’s residual is a quarter of SPMe’s (11.0 against 42.8 Wh/kg) and SPMe’s tracks its own minimum salt concentration (Spearman −0.82). The worst-case cost formula built on it predicted screen against GP-EI on only 8 of 16 pool sizes (refuted). Milestone 4 (search replay) replays 12 search methods on the cached benchmark, 30 pools of 64 designs, each simulation charged its measured wall time: screening every candidate with the plain SPM (100 cycles) or a 2-cycle DFN run and verifying in screen order reaches a design within 1% of the best 100-cycle DFN score in a median 153 or 160 s, against 220 s for GP-EI on DFN; the 10-cycle DFN screen takes 253 s (pre-registered H7, that it would need a third of GP-EI's time, refuted), successive halving over DFN cycles 247 s (185 s if runs resume), and milestone 1's trust flag cuts SPMe screening from 700 to 418 s. On pools of 96 GP-EI catches up, so whole-pool screening suits small candidate sets. Milestone 2 (dense benchmark) runs 128 fresh space-filling (Sobol) designs for 100 cycles under SPM, SPMe and DFN (384 runs, every cycle kept): a 10-cycle DFN run ranks the designs by their 100-cycle DFN Wh/kg at Spearman 0.962 (95% 0.932–0.977), against 0.641 (0.480–0.789) for a full 100-cycle SPMe run, at the same wall time (3.6 s against 3.7 s), and its top 10 contain the DFN-best design, which SPMe ranks 41st. Unplanned: the plain SPM ranks better than SPMe (0.955; 0.984 against 0.769 over the 121 designs SPMe completes), though it over-scores the best design by 20 Wh/kg, and 15 of 128 designs (12%) are mis-scored by SPMe by over 25%. Milestone 2a, the same question on the 49 stratified designs of energy-cell-dfn: 10-cycle DFN 0.977 against 0.834 for 100-cycle SPMe (paired bootstrap difference 0.138, 95% 0.057–0.271), and a linear fade extrapolation fails (Spearman 0.01). Milestone 1: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration classifies the designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 on the 49 (0.994 on the 128, whole-run minimum). Re-runs reproduce the committed SPMe and DFN scores exactly. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, costs timed on one design and one 4-core machine, no measured cell for these designs.
